video_goal: Demonstrate the precise folding sequence to create a Suzanne dart-style paper airplane.
required_subjects_and_props: Standard A4 sheet of paper, flat wooden table, hands

outline_steps.visual_action: Two hands place a crisp, standard A4 sheet of paper flat on a wooden table, orienting it vertically.
Hands fold the paper in half lengthwise, pressing a thumb firmly along the left edge to create a sharp center crease.
Hands unfold the paper flat against the table, revealing the vertical center crease running down the middle.
The right hand folds the top-right corner down so its inner edge aligns perfectly with the center crease.
The left hand folds the top-left corner down to meet the right edge, forming a sharp triangular peak at the top of the paper.
Hands take the newly formed diagonal edge on the right and fold it inward so it lies flush against the center crease.
Hands repeat the diagonal fold on the left side, pressing down to create a narrow, elongated dart shape.
The index finger and thumb fold the sharp top point down about one inch, creating the signature blunt nose of the Suzanne style.
Hands fold the entire paper in half along the original center crease, enclosing the blunt nose fold inside the two halves.
The right hand folds the top flap down to create the first wing, leaving a half-inch gap at the bottom fold to form the fuselage.
Hands flip the plane over and fold the second wing down, perfectly aligning its outer edge with the first wing.
Thumbs pinch the outer trailing edges of both wings, folding them up slightly to form half-inch vertical winglets.
Hands open the wings outward, adjusting them to a slight upward 'V' angle (dihedral), and hold the finished Suzanne dart-style plane toward the camera.
